#4904. The Best Epilators for At-Home Hair Removal in 2026, According to Experts

Here's why they're better than waxing, shaving, or a laser.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Fall’s signature cool, crisp temperatures have me reevaluating more than just my wardrobe. My skincare routine is due for a seasonal refresh—but one beauty ritual that I won’t skip is body hair removal. There’s nothing wrong with body hair, of course. But if you’re like me and prefer smooth, dolphin-like skin brushing against your matching workout sets and cozy sweater dresses, then chances are that you’ve tried a slew of hair removal methods.

Shaving is cheap and easy, but it requires daily maintenance. Depilatory hair removal creams are convenient, but they can easily irritate sensitive skin. Waxing results last up to six weeks, but the discomfort can also be unpleasant for those with sensitive skin. Some of our editors adore laser hair removal devices, but they’ll set you back at least $300. Many aren’t designed with Brown and Black skin tones like mine.

However, we’re all in on one hair removal technique: epilators. They resemble electric razors, but instead of trimming hairs at the surface, they pluck them from the root for long-lasting, smooth skin. Because the hair-free results last for two to four weeks, epilators are a great alternative to shaving and hair removal creams. Repeated sessions slow down hair growth, and your unwanted strands will be finer when they regrow, says dermatologist Hadley King, MD. They’re also gentler than laser hair removal devices, which is why Dr. King recommends them for anyone with sensitive skin or who isn't a good fit for laser hair removal.

My favorites start at just $9, so you can enjoy hair-free skin without putting a major dent in your beauty budget ahead of the holiday season. Plus, many of our recommendations are sold on Amazon, meaning you can take full advantage of the retailer’s signature two-day Prime shipping and enjoy hair-free legs before your upcoming weekend plans.

WH editors haven’t met a Braun device we don’t love—and this top-rated epilator is no exception. I love that it’s equipped with a wide, flexible head that flawlessly bends along the curves of my kneecaps, underarms, and my bikini line. Even better? It features an impressive number of micro-grip tweezers, which are much slimmer than traditional tweezers in the motor to ensure I get the closest hair removal possible. While it sounds intimidating, the sheer number of tweezers sped up my hair removal process.

This wet-dry device has an impressive 50-minute runtime which allows me to remove unwanted body hair over several sessions without worrying about it dying mid-epilating. It also has a relatively quick charging time of just an hour, which is shorter than other epilators I’ve come across in my research and testing process.

Despite the lightweight feel, I like how sturdy this device is and that it doesn’t easily slip out of my grip. Plus, it's waterproof so you can use your new epilator in the shower without worrying about it cranking out mid-shave.

And while a small detail, this device has a built-in “smartlight” that illuminates your skin while epilating, solidifying it as a must-have for women who like dimmer lighting while showering but still want to see what they're doing.

Truthfully, the only bummer about this device is that it’s the most expensive recommendation. However, we think its performance makes it worth it.

Love the idea of a facial epilator but you don’t need the face cleansing brush or facial toning attachments? Reach for this $21 find from Remington. (To achieve the best results, your facial hair should be no longer than 5 mm.)

Remington includes a protective cap to guard the tweezers against damage when not in use, while the cleaning brush removes any hair buildup that can cause your device to temporarily stop working. It’s also portable and compact enough to toss into your purse or toiletry bag. Plus, we appreciate that it’s completely cordless and battery operated (it includes one AA battery), making it easy to maneuver for tight spots.

The only downside with this device is that it can only be used dry, so it’s best to use after cleansing your face.

When you need a small-yet-mighty epilator that cleans up targeted areas like your bikini line, this palm-sized power tool is your girl. And it's only $40!

While it’s recommended to wax hair that’s at least 0.25 inches long (6.35 mm), this Philips device is designed to remove hairs as short as 0.5 mm from the root, so it’s much easier to remain hair-free with this tool. This is especially noteworthy given the fantastic price point. Despite its small size (a mere 4.72 x 2.36 inches), it can be used on your entire body, including your sensitive bikini line.

Epilating newbies will also love that this pretty pink device is gentler than other alternatives because it includes a massage cap that minimizes pain while in use. So bikini epilating won’t be as painful when you use this device.

Beyond the incredible price, we also appreciate how quickly this device works. It took McMahon only 10 minutes to remove unwanted hair from both of her lower legs. We originally highlighted the more affordable $80 version of this device, then the upgraded 8000 model. However the battery-powered Braun Facespa Pro 911 is designed exclusively for your face so if you’re dealing with pesky chin hairs or vellus hair a.k.a. the fine, short peach fuzz above your lips or on your cheeks and sideburns, then this is for you.

It also works as a cleansing brush and vibrating head (swap in the silver-tipped attachment) that helps your facial toner easily penetrate into your skin. The micro-vibration head also works with your face moisturizer or facial serum. And thanks to the automatic smart head detection you don’t have to fuss around changing any settings.

It can also be used wet and dry, so you can use it in the shower if you desire or in front of your vanity mirror when it suits you (note that it is water-resistant, not waterproof, however).

Hear me out: the reader-favorite Foreo Luna 4 Facial Cleansing Brush that doubles as a face massager is $200. Face massage wand prices can greatly vary. Ultimately, if you’re maxing out at $150 opt for this device to enjoy the massaging and hair removal benefits.

If you need razor-sharp precision, this device has the smallest head on the list. It’s designed to quickly, safely, and easily pluck away multiple stray hairs in your eyebrow area. You can still use this on your face, lips, chin, and even nose, but it’ll just take a little longer because the tip is so small. And whether you’ve got a few stray hairs, bushy brows, or even a unibrow, this device has you covered.

We’re impressed that such an affordable device doesn’t cut corners. Instead, it has hypoallergenic stainless steel blades that minimize the risk of redness, irritation, and scratches. Like pricier alternatives, this just under-$9 find also has a built-in LED light to illuminate your eyebrows so you can ensure even the tiniest, lightest strands are found and eliminated. It’s also the most affordable waterproof hair removal device on our list, though only the shaver head is waterproof, so it’s best to use in a dry setting.

This device comes with a USB cord that you can plug into your laptop, along with a single replacement blade that can last between three to six months, depending on usage. Even if you use this tool twice a month, it’s like you’re spending $1.50 per month over the course of half a year. Not too shabby!

Rest easy and reach for this device when you want to use an affordable epilator from a trusted brand that’s great for beginners. Braun is one of the most legit hair removal companies in the game, but don’t just take our word for it. This device earned the most Amazon reviews (a casual 4.2-star average from nearly 22,000) among our expert-vetted recommendations.

So what makes this sub-$40 epilator worth it? Thanks to interchangeable heads, you can epilate, trim, and shave with a single device. You can use the gentle trimmer to cut down longer body hairs, an epilator to remove them from the root, and the shaver attachment to clean up any areas when you’re in a pinch. Swapping out the attachments is seamless—and the shaver is awesome for days I want smooth skin, but my body hair isn't long enough for epilating.

Beginners will especially love the trimmer because it doesn't irritate our sensitive skin. And the epilator head has a built-in massage roller that helps minimize any discomfort. While it's not as effective as our best overall epilator, it gets the job done by removing all of our unwanted body hair in around 30 minutes. Most importantly, the pain is rather minimal. Not too shabby for a compact, travel-friendly pick!

Like our No. 1 pick, this more affordable tool is also equipped with a smartlight feature to illuminate your skin and spotlight inconspicuous body hairs. It’s also equipped with two speed settings, making it helpful for beginners and novices alike.

The biggest downside with this tool is that it’s not designed to remove unwanted facial hair. That said, you can pluck away rogue chin hairs or reach for the Amazon bestselling Kitsch dermaplaning tool that trims your brows and shaves your face to reveal smoother skin.

Epilators are unique because they’re equipped with built-in tweezers to pluck hairs from the root.

The smaller heads have fewer tweezers, but they're fantastic for targeted areas like the face, underarms, and bikini line.

Larger epilator heads are better for covering bigger areas like your legs. Having a lot of tweezers helps speed up your hair removal routine, but it also means you’ll have a more painful experience because it’s plucking dozens of hairs at a time. But like ripping a bandage off a hairy arm, it’s uncomfortable at first, but not too rough. And FWIW, Dr. King promises the pain level noticeably improves after multiple sessions. So be brave and patient, and it’ll all be over before you know it.

For the most effective hair removal, your body hair should be about the length of a sprinkle or grain of rice (about 0.25 inches or 6.35 mm). This standard for epilators is the same as waxing and sugaring. When your hair is too short, it's challenging for the epilator to grasp and remove the strands. You also don't want them to be longer than about two rice grains to help prevent hairs from getting tangled and minimize pain. Everyone's hair regrowth is different, but for most people, stubble typically occurs within one to two weeks.

It sounds like a small detail, but also consider the power source.

If you have minimal outlets in your home, then battery-powered makes sense. However, the hidden cost of replacing batteries can start to add up within the year. That said, all of the featured battery-operated devices in this story include a battery to help offset the long-term cost.

These devices are great because you won’t have to worry about them cranking out mid-epilating, but honestly the cords can get in the way. If you’ve got the extra funds, it’s best to invest in a cordless device so you can remove your unwanted body hair without stretching in odd positions or sitting on your bedroom floor. That said, there are some stellar corded options, including the relatively affordable $40 Philips Epilator Series 2000.

Water-resistant devices can be used wet or dry, so the cordless option can be used in your shower and the corded version works on your damp body if you prefer. Most aren’t waterproof, except the Braun Epilator Silk-épil 9 Flex 9-481 Beauty Set and the epilator head on the Colordiary Eyebrow Hair Remover.

As our beauty editor, I’m constantly on the hunt for the best products, and spend the vast majority of my time testing and reviewing the latest drops. I also regularly consult dermatologists about all things beauty, which is exactly what I did to kick off the selection process for our best epilators story. After talking with Dr. King (she’s one of my most trusted dermatological experts), I asked about her recommendations and insights into shopping for epilators. Then, our team tested several of her picks and compared them to some of the other epilators in our beauty closet.

We've been testing epilators since March 2021, and over time we've evaluated dozens of newer models with various features until we settled on these seven winners. In the years since, we've kept a close eye on the latest launches across all price points and have updated this story at least yearly to share our honest thoughts. For our most recent update, we tried 12 epilators and determined these seven are worthy of a place in our routine—and we're confident they'll equally impress you as well.

Over the last six weeks we've been trying a slew of options and kept the number of tweezers, power source, and water resistance in mind. Next, we paid attention to the number of attachments. We prioritized accessories that helped alleviate discomfort to ensure we have less intimidating options for beginners. Next, we considered each epilator's ease of use, noise level, grip strength, comfort, and efficacy at removing hair. Our team used these devices in our real lives and ahead of important events, like weddings, birthdays, and after exercise.

To narrow down the list even further, I recruited Women's Health colleagues, including Assistant Social Media Editor Isabel McMahon, to join the testing process. I also carefully vetted all of the top-rated picks across Amazon, Ulta, and Sephora. I also considered pricing. While yes, the top pick is over $250, it’s from Braun, one of the most-trusted names in the hair removal game. It also earned major snaps from McMahon and me. And FWIW, our other picks are $140 and under, with some in the sweet $10-$40 range.

If you’re interested in giving epilating a shot, the above are some highly reviewed options that will get you on your way to smooth, bare skin.

These devices look like chunky electric razors and are either manual like a traditional women’s razor or powered by batteries or an electrical outlet. When you run the device across your body, tiny tweezers pluck away unwanted body hair. So yes, the initial hair removal process will be a tad uncomfy, but the smooth results are so worth it, says Dr. King.

Like all other hair removal techniques, using an epilator is all about skin prep. Dr. King recommends a gentle physical exfoliation, such as a body scrub, gloves, mitt, loofah, or brush, before epilation. (Psst: I’ve been using Nécessaire The Body Exfoliant since 2019 and haven’t looked back since.) "This will help to expose hairs so they can be picked up by the epilator, and it also helps decrease the risk of ingrown hairs," says Dr. King.

#4902. The 8 Best Natural Deodorants for Men in 2026, Tested by Grooming Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Sticks that are gentler on your skin and the environment.

SUMMER HEAT MAY be gone, but you still need deodorant. While soaps and body wash rinse away sweat and grime, deodorant keeps odor at bay throughout the day by masking funky smells and killing odor-causing bacteria. So, it’s a crucial part of the defense—no matter the season. If you have sensitive skin or prefer eco-conscious products, natural deodorant is your best bet.

Traditional deodorants use ingredients that may irritate skin or disrupt your body’s natural sweat response, like parabens, phthalates, or, most notably, aluminum. While the FDA does list aluminum as a safe ingredient to be used in deodorants or antiperspirants, to be clear, those with sensitive skin can still find it irritating.

This is because the ingredient can cause inflammation leading to itchiness and rash, as well as worsening dry skin conditions like eczema, says dermatologist Dr. Anna Chacon, MD, FAAD. Not to mention, aluminum can inhibit the body’s natural sweat response by actively plugging pores with heavy metals that stop sweat from being excreted, she says.

Still, there is also a lot of noise out there regarding aluminum contributing to Alzheimer’s disease or cancer, but none have been substantiated. Still, natural alternatives skip this risk and instead rely on plant-based ingredients like essential oils, probiotics, and starches to combat odor and moisture.

Quick reminder: Deodorants do not block sweat; they mask body odor. Only an antiperspirant will do this, but there are no natural antiperspirants, as aluminum is required to plug sweat glands. So, natural deodorants are used as an alternative to both. Plus, they tend to be better for the environment by often using biodegradable ingredients or eco-friendly packaging to reduce waste and plastic pollution.

With all of this in mind, it’s fair to wonder why natural deodorants aren’t the norm. Well, these products have a bit of a bad reputation when it comes to their ability to last as long as traditional aluminum-filled options. While this does hold true for many natural deodorants, there are options on this list that last just as long, and in the case of Ursa Major Hoppin' Fresh Natural Deodorant, which lasts well over 24 hours, outperforms most traditional deodorants.

Salt and Stone incorporates hyaluronic acid and seaweed extract in its natural deodorant to eliminate bad odor, prevent underarm darkening, and deliver intense hydration, which is crucial for preventing funky smells, maintaining health skin, and ensuring proper sweat gland functioning. Not to mention, these ingredients will keep you smelling fresh from morning to night.

While most deodorants (natural and otherwise) have alcohol, which can cause blocked pores, irritation, and dryness, this vegan option leaves it out of the formula. But what really separates Salt and Stone from other brands is its killer natural fragrances.

The santal and vetiver scent smells so good; I’ve often worn it in lieu of cologne. This fresh, subtle sandalwood smell lasts too—all day. The lightweight formula glides on smoothly and soothes my skin. It’s the only natural deodorant I’ve tried that straight up outperforms many of my go-to standard sticks.

It never stains, never aggravates my skin, and rarely needs to be reapplied (only after working out or something especially sweaty). Whether you’re looking for a natural deodorant that smells great or one that’ll keep you protected from odor, Salt and Stone is the best option.

Schmidt’s is a natural deodorant that skips the common bacteria-absorbing and odor-neutralizing baking soda, but still delivers. Packed with skin-friendly ingredients like magnesium and charcoal, it glides on smoothly, dries to a matte finish, and works for virtually all skin types, including sensitive. I have sensitive pits and have faced zero irritation when using this stuff.

The crisp citrus and spearmint scent feels fresh without being overpowering. With just a couple of swipes, you get all-day odor control. I’ll put this on after a pre-work shower and still smell it the next morning when I wake up. Pro tip: Warm the stick briefly against your skin before applying for a smoother glide. While it won’t block sweat, arrowroot and magnesium help absorb moisture and fight funk.

Ursa Major Hoppin' Fresh Natural Deodorant is one of the most reliable natural options out there. It goes on smooth, never stains, and keeps me smelling fresh with its crisp peppermint eucalyptus scent. The formula does use baking soda, so those with sensitive skin may want to look elsewhere. However, it also includes kaolin clay, which absorbs sweat, and hops—just like your favorite beer—to fight odor by neutralizing the growth of odor-causing bacteria (but not sweat, to be clear).

When I use this stick, my skin stays calm and clear. I’ve found that it can ward off odor in the midst of the sweatiest, stickiest summer outings, like a long run or a day at the beach. Plus, I’ve had a Hoppin' Fresh stick last over three months. This thing’s a legit money saver.

Most natural deodorants, understandably, use a lot of fragrance to help mask odor. Somehow, this fragrance-free version neutralizes stink without the aid of added scent. It could be the probiotics in the formula that help to maintain good (non-stinky) bacteria. Or it could be voodoo, who knows? This Hume helped keep B.O. at bay during even the hottest days outside. While it doesn't stop sweat like an antiperspirant, of course, the fragrance-free formula does keep you smelling fresh and clean, somehow. It’s just more like that fresh-out-of-the-shower clean, rather than cologned-up clean.

Some natural deodorants ask you to change your routine—they don’t apply as easily as the traditional ones you’re used to. Native, however, goes on smoothly and doesn’t need to be warmed up or applied with your fingers. This clean vanilla and sandalwood scent is fresh without smelling fake.

The warm, woodsy fragrance is clean and masculine without being overpowering. It goes on cleanly, without any residue, thanks to the twist-up stick. Often natural deodorants, they have a looser texture, but this is the closest to the feel of a traditional stick.

So, if you’re going natural for the first time, it’s the perfect place to start. The included arrowroot and tea tree oil will leave you feeling fresh, and I’ve had one stick last about two months with daily use. This is another one with baking soda, however, so those sensitive might see a reaction (though I didn’t!).

Fighting tough stains can be, well, tough. Enter Malin and Goetz's natural deodorant. With a unique combination of citronellyl and eucalyptus extract, this transparent formula won't leave any traces of residue on your favorite garments. It’s not the strongest deodorant, to be clear, as it will start to fade around the 12-hour mark.

But the cooling scent lasts longer than others that need to be reapplied often. Plus, the lightweight application goes on clear and seemingly evaporates in seconds. I’ve worn black T-shirts at the same time as wearing this deodorant without a trace.

Humble Brands Plastic-Free deodorant is made with just four clean ingredients plus essential oils, and it skips all the junk: no aluminum, parabens, dyes, or synthetic fragrances. The Mountain Lavender scent is earthy and calming, though it may be a bit too strong for those who don’t love an essential oil scent.

What really sold me, however, is the packaging—completely plastic-free, biodegradable, and even the ink is plant-based. Sure, it keeps me dry and odor-free all day, but I also feel good knowing it’s as gentle on my skin as it is on the planet. It’s no wonder Jason Momoa chose Humble to help launch his first deodorant.

Read More: Inside Jason Momoa’s Humble Deodorant

No brand nails masculine, earthy scents quite like Dr. Squatch, and its natural deodorant is no different. The pine tar-scented option, especially, nails the peaceful fragrance of woods at dawn. In fact, it’s the closest I’ve gotten to the indescribable smell of waking up after a night camping in the Sequoia National Forest.

That being said, the deodorant isn’t confirmed to be entirely 100 percent natural. While every ingredient listed could be naturally derived, the brand only confirms 98 percent natural. Still, I never had a reaction with my sensitive skin, and there certainly isn’t any aluminum in the formula. While the application is clean and lightweight, Dr. Squatch also packs one of the longest-lasting scents on this list (up to 48 hours, in my experience).

Again, natural deodorants will never contain aluminum to block sweat. Instead, they use sweat-absorbing ingredients like arrowroot powder, clay, or tapioca starch to manage moisture without stopping sweat entirely. If you see aluminum listed, it’s not truly natural.

Many natural formulas include baking soda to fight odor and absorb wetness, but it can also irritate sensitive skin, causing redness or itching. For those with sensitive skin, baking soda-free options are a safer choice. Natural deodorants also feature soothing moisturizers like coconut oil or other plant-based oils, plus fragrances from essential oils to keep you fresh.

Most natural deodorants mask odor with either synthetic fragrances, like limonene (found in orange peels) and linalool (from plants like lavender and basil), or natural essential oils like lavender, tea tree, or lemon. Neither is inherently better, just comes down to what scent you’re into. But keep in mind that while stronger scents may last longer, there is no guarantee for better odor protection.

Many natural deodorants include extra ingredients to fight odor after the scent fades, including bacterial absorbents like arrowroot, cornstarch, potassium alum, or zinc. If you have sensitive skin, heavy fragrances can still cause irritation, so opt for lighter or unscented formulas.

If you’re going the natural deodorant route for environmental reasons, you’ll probably also want to look for cruelty-free options, which means that the product was not tested on animals. While many grooming products are tested on animals, natural deodorants often prioritize more ethical practices, choosing not to test on animals as part of their commitment to a clean, conscious lifestyle, Dr. Chacon says.

As a grooming editor who was raised on The Grateful Dead not far from Woodstock, I’m intimately familiar with natural, eco-friendly alternatives. For this story, I considered personal favorites and options with high ratings on major e-commerce sites like Amazon. Ultimately, I landed on over 20 natural deodorants to test throughout the past year.

I wore each for at least a week, judging scent, staying power, the way it felt on my skin, and how well they held up through workouts, stress, and overall sweat. From that hands-on testing, these are the eight best natural deodorants for men that actually perform.

The most common argument that natural deodorants are better for you is centered around aluminum. Some claim that aluminum is linked with Alzheimer’s disease, but older studies have been discredited, and there has been no discernible link found between aluminum and Alzheimer’s, according to the Alzheimer’s Association.

It’s also been suggested that aluminum can increase your risk of cancer, particularly breast cancer in women. Dr. Chacon says that more research to determine a concrete link between either is needed, but early studies showing greater aluminum buildup in the brains of Alzheimer’s sufferers is concerning.

There is also usually conversation around preservative parabens, which some claim are linked to cancer as well, and other chemical ingredients that natural deodorants omit from their formulas. While, again, no studies have proven that these ingredients are directly linked to illnesses like cancer, many people like to err on the side of caution.

Apart from all this, traditional deodorants often contain ingredients that can irritate skin, like certain kinds of alcohol or artificial fragrances. Most natural deodorants seek to solve this problem by using naturally derived ingredients that may be more gentle on the skin. The bottom line is that there is no evidence that natural deodorants are better for you than traditional deodorants or antiperspirants; some simply prefer them for their lifestyle and skin.

#4900. The 6 Best Undereye Patches, Tested and Reviewed by Dermatologists and Beauty Editors

The entire Women's Health team swears by them.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’m always up late doomscrolling TikTok and The White Lotus subreddit for season 4 theories. (Natasha Rothwell hive, stand up!) The only problem? Those late nights mean I have dark circles and puffiness in the morning (boo!). While I'm a huge fan of undereye creams, sometimes I get bored and need to switch things up. Enter undereye patches. They're a fast fix for dryness, puffiness, and dark circles—and even help me fake eight hours of sleep. "The skin under the eyes is prone to changes related to aging skin, such as fine lines, and conditions like dryness and discoloration," says dermatologist Brendan Camp, MD. In just 10 to 20 minutes, undereye patches temporarily hydrate the delicate skin and help me look refreshed. Plus, they're super cute and add a fun touch to my selfies, even if they're shared to just my Close Friends circle on Instagram Stories.

Like any other skin care product, eye masks really get their power from their ingredients, some of which are typically hyaluronic acid, vitamin C, niacinamide, and caffeine.

“Eye patches incorporate key ingredients like hyaluronic acid to boost moisture, peptides to firm, ceramides to strengthen the skin barrier, caffeine to help reduce puffiness, and niacinamide to reduce discoloration,” says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD.

As with any beauty product, there are always a few things to consider before making the investment. Since these masks are mostly advertised for their ability to soothe and hydrate, you'll want to check the hydrating and firming ingredients, and keep your expectations realistic since results are usually temporary. Here's what to look out for.

For starters, look for key ingredients such as aloe, chamomile, cucumber, green tea, glycerin, or hyaluronic acid. You're less likely to come across vitamin C and retinol, but it's a plus if you do. Patches with a cellulose gel material can also prevent them from sliding off your face (a con I often deal with and try to avoid as much as possible).

Not only is the skin under your eyes thinner and more delicate than in other areas of your face, but it’s also where lymphatic fluid drainage occurs, says dermatologist Lauren Penzi, MD. It can also show more blood vessels, and in turn, make dark circles appear more visible, says Dr. Garshick. Most eye masks are created to reduce fine lines, undereye darkness, and wrinkles while giving your skin the boost of moisture it needs. The overall effect of these patches is to revive and hydrate, which is why so many people use them to get a more refreshed look.

Many people complain about looking tired, and eye patches are a nice, quick fix. Still, it's important to be realistic about the kind of results you'll get in just one or two uses. So, you’ll want to zero in on the reason you’re buying patches, says Dr. Camp. For example, you can target puffiness by rocking undereye patches infused with caffeine or green tea while getting ready for work, says Dr. Camp.

As a member of the beauty team at Women’s Health, I’m constantly on the hunt for the best products and spend a lot of my time testing and reviewing the latest drops. I frequently consult skin experts, which is exactly what I did to kick off my selection process here. I consulted five New York-based dermatologists and had them give their recommendations with insight on why these undereye masks are so splurge-worthy. Then, I tested several of their picks and compared them to some of the other undereye masks available in our beauty closet.To narrow down the list even further, I got a few other members of team WH, including Addison Aloian, Lily Wohlner, Brian Underwood, and Danielle Jackson, to get in on the testing process. Ingredients, price, and overall efficacy were taken into account to determine which would be best for a wide range of needs and preferences.Here are the fruits of our labor.

After testing tons of undereye masks, this one takes the cake for best overall. Why? It's the most hydrating option on this list and it doesn't slip off your face, which is super hard to find in an undereye mask.

ICYMI, Wander Beauty basically started the undereye mask trend. This OG mask is made with peptides, amino acids, and hyaluronic acid to improve your skin's texture, tone, and hydration. It's also expert-approved by Dr. Garshick and dermatologist Dendy Engelman, MD. "I love that this mask is made with three different layers that allow the formula to penetrate the skin deeply and prevent it from sliding off the face, so you can multitask while you wear it," says Dr. Engelman.

Wander Beauty patches are as effective as they are Instagrammable. I’ve been a fan of the rose gold and yellow gold patches for five years, and all of my beauty editor friends gush over them. They brighten, hydrate, and plump up my fine lines. They also contain calendula extract and aloe vera to help reduce puffiness. Ahem, hi holiday parties and upcoming travel—I’m looking at you.

These pretty patches have three unique layers: the surface's foil retains heat and prevents evaporation, the middle grips to prevent slippage, and the base delivers moisturizing glycerin and depuffing calendula extract. For an extra soothing experience, I like to leave mine in the fridge. Cool temperatures help shrink blood vessels under the eyes, so dark circles appear lighter and puffiness minimizes, dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD, said in our guide to undereye skin care.

That said, the construction of this mask consists of super light and flexible material versus the conventional plastic material found in a lot of other eye patches that were tested, giving this product a high-quality feel.

I would be remiss if I didn't mention my personal fave patch from Patchology. It contains hyaluronic acid (hi, hydrated, plump skin) and feels super cool under the eyes to de-puff and smooth out that area.

Patchology is fantastic for targeting lines, says dermatologist Anar Mikailov, MD. He mentions that there's resveratrol, a natural antioxidant found in grapes that helps improve barrier function, and other antioxidants that provide protection against oxidizing agents that can visibly age the skin by causing wrinkles. There’s also antioxidant-rich strawberry extract, which helps brighten dark circles.

After using this patch, I also noticed my undereye area was less puffy and more luminous. My only con was that the mask slides out of place after a while, but it’s still epic to use and totally worth incorporating into your routine. My hack is to use these patches while lying down in bed to prevent any slipping.

This undereye mask is basically an expert at reducing puffy, tired-looking eyes thanks to its cooling effects. It also temporarily plumps up my fine lines with hydrating hyaluronic acid.

This option comes with a lot of serum, so it may slip down your face over time. But, feel free to go ahead and massage that extra serum into your undereye area—that little bit of massaging can help assist with lymphatic drainage and further reduce puffiness. Need even more convincing? Celebs like Jessica Alba post about this mask on her Instagram story time and time again, noting that she's a major fan.

Most masks on this list only need 10 minutes on the skin, but this one should stay on for up to 20. Although, 20 minutes fly by when you have a good book in hand (pro tip!).

These eye masks from Live Tinted are packed with copper peptides and banana extract (hi, Ashton Hall!) to reduce puffiness and smooth fine lines. They also reduce puffiness after just a few uses and leave skin looking glowy and feeling hydrated.

And because these patches help soften and smooth your delicate undereye area, Aloian relies on them for makeup prep. "Not only is the patch super cute—it's shaped like a sun—but it also genuinely hydrates and brightens my undereye area," she says. These patches make Aloian feel confident going makeup free because of the glow they leave behind, but it's just as helpful on days when she wants a dewy base before applying concealer.

Along with a mix of peptides to help stimulate collagen production, this eye mask contains niacinamide, bakuchiol, caffeine, and vitamin C. Bakuchiol is a great retinol alternative that helps stimulate collagen production, says Dr. Mikailov.

Wohlner also gave this patch a try and loves how flexible it is under the eye. However, she did note that it does tend to slip down the face because it's super thin.

This vitamin C-packed eye patch is perfect for helping brighten up the undereye area while reducing signs of aging and puffiness with the help of caffeine.

Yeah, it's a little pricier, but trust that it's totally worth it if you have the budget. The gel patches are super easy to apply. Plus, they can reduce discoloration and fine lines within just a few weeks. Sometimes I'm wary of products with vitamin C in them because the smell can be a bit aggressive, but these are just right.

Derms also deem this patch worth the money. "The key ingredient in this mask is THD Ascorbate Vitamin C, which is 50 times more powerful than other forms of vitamin C," says Dr. Engelman. THD is especially good for surface dark spots that need brightening rather than deeper dark circles, says Dr. Mikailov.

It's worth noting that these dry up around the 10-minute mark, and while they stay on really well, the edges break off easily if you try to move the masks around a few minutes after the initial application.

As the name suggests, this patch is meant to soothe tired-looking eyes. So, for those of you who have a lot of sleepless nights or are just night owls at heart, this is your winner. Infused with caffeine, niacinamide, and hyaluronic acid, these work overtime to reduce puffiness and dark circles.

"I often recommend Peace Out’s acne patch for the face, but I also love the brand’s eye patches," says Dr. Engelman. "It's so effective at quickly bringing down puffiness and brightening and smoothing the under-eyes." The patch is biodegradable and made with biocellulose, which helps the formula deeply penetrate the skin, says Dr. Engelman.

These patches fit snugly under my eyes, so I could wear them while doing my eye makeup. They also did a great job of catching eyeshadow fallout that would normally ruin my undereye concealer. Another pro? Unlike most gel patches, they weren’t completely soaked in serum, which can make the process a bit messy. Instead, they had just the right amount for ample hydration. After the initial use, I noticed my undereyes were softer and brighter, and I’d slowly reach for these patches for special occasions.

I’m not the only fan on WH’s beauty team. “I have very sensitive skin, so I'm always cautious when it comes to trying things out, but this didn't give me any issues,” says tester Sabrina Talbert. “It also doesn't have much of a scent, which put my mind at ease since fragrance tends to be an early indicator that my skin might not like a product.”

These patches are on the larger side, so they feel a bit bulky. They also need to be slightly adjusted because they slide down a little bit over 15 minutes, but honestly, they’re such minor cons that Talbert continues using them.

#4899. 7 Best Lumbar Pillows Bolster Your Back and Bedscape (2026)

Though a lumbar pillow is typically the last detail in making a bed, it’s often the first thing you or a guest will notice. Because it’s long and low, its best suited to the space in front of loftier throw pillows, making a horizon line across your bedscape, and it can bring in a color or texture the rest of the room is vying for. The shape turns up all over AD’s archives, including in supermodel Paloma Elsesser’s Brooklyn home and this classically decorated Southern house.

A lumbar pillow can mean two things: a firm or cushioned gel pillow designed to support the lower back, or an elegant decorative detail among your bedding. While we like both, we’ll leave the Cushion Lab’s best-of for another day. Here, we’re focused on a more inspirational lineup, between linen, wool, velvet, and cotton lumbar pillows that pull a bed and sofa together (and still give your lower back something to lean on in an accent chair). Below are the seven we like best.

Sometimes one pillow is all a bed really needs. West Elm’s oversized linen pillow cover has the scale to anchor a queen or king bed on its own, creating a clean, pulled-together look without a full stack of throw pillows. The linen keeps it loose, making it especially well-suited to coastal, minimalist, modern farmhouse, and casual contemporary spaces.

This pillow is all about texture. Its dimensional surface gives a sofa or bed a more layered, considered look without relying on a loud print or saturated color. In other words, its style will speak volumes even when paired with quieter neutrals.

At 48 inches, Quince’s velvet lumbar is long enough to span a queen bed with nothing else in front of it, and the cotton pile catches light in a way linen won’t. The glacier blue reads cool and a little silvery against white or oatmeal bedding. It’s dry clean only, and the insert is sold separately.

Color is the point with this Athena cushion. Rather than fading quietly into the background, this lumbar pillow is designed to bring energy to a room, whether it’s breaking up the monotony of a neutral living room or adding contrast to a more restrained bedding scheme. It’s the kind of accent that makes a pillow arrangement feel more collected, playful, and intentional.

A little color can go a long way, especially in the form of Pendleton’s Turquoise Crosses Lumbar Pillow. Its vivid palette and geometric pattern give neutral furniture or a plain accent chair an instant lift. For anyone drawn to Southwestern-inspired textiles, this pick brings just enough graphic punch without crowding the rest of the room.

The Mendocino cover is made up of hand-dyed washed linen, so the color shifts slightly across the surface instead of sitting flat. What separates it from the other linen picks here is the fringe: three-inch knotted tassels run along two sides, which give a simple lumbar some movement at the ends of a sofa or bed. Nota bene: the insert is sold separately.

Washed linen has a way of making a room feel more relaxed and breezy, which is exactly the appeal of Brooklinen’s pillow cover. The simple design is easy to fold into an existing pillow arrangement, while the softly textured fabric and choice of vibrant hues keep it from feeling too plain.

A lumbar pillow is a long, rectangular cushion designed to support the lower back. The term describes two different products: one is the ergonomic back support pillow, often memory foam, made for an office chair or car seat. The other is the decorative version on this list, which works as an accent piece on beds, sofas, benches, and accent chairs. Their shape makes them especially useful for layering with standard square throw pillows, adding dimension without making a space feel cluttered.

One of the easiest ways to style a lumbar pillow is to place it in front of larger pillows or shams on a bed. On a sofa or accent chair, a lumbar pillow can serve as a single focal point or be paired with smaller throw pillows in complementary colors, patterns, or textures. For a more polished look, choose a lumbar pillow that either picks up a color already in the room or brings in a contrasting texture, like linen, wool, velvet, or tassels.

For lower back support, a lumbar pillow goes in the curve between your back and the back of a sofa, reading chair, or recliner chair. Keep in mind a firmer, fuller back pillow will likely do more for your posture than a soft, decorative one. For styling, it can also be centered across a bed, layered in front of sleeping pillows, or placed on a bench for extra comfort and visual interest. Oversized lumbar pillows work especially well on queen and king beds because they can anchor the entire pillow arrangement with one clean horizontal line.

#4897. The 8 Best Slip-On Walking Shoes, According to Our Editors

Looking to get out the door quicker? Don’t let laces slip you up.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SLIDING INTO A pair of slip-on walking shoes might be the easiest thing you’ll do all day. This footwear was built for speed and convenience, making it an accessory that deserves valuable real estate by your door.

Slip-on walking shoes have a rocky history—older versions had a looser fit, raising the risk of instability and friction, especially with higher mileage. But newer designs use no-tie laces, sock liners, pull tabs, and collapsible heels to create a custom fit that rivals what you’ll get with traditional laces.

These shoes are an obvious choice if you have dexterity issues, but they're also just convenient for everyone looking for an easy pair of walking shoes. Slip-on walking shoes also offer more structure than other laceless shoe designs, which has earned them a fanbase with podiatrists. “They are typically a much better option than flip-flops or slides because they provide more stability and keep the foot properly secured,” says Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois.

Nicole Graf, DPM, founder of Lexington Podiatry and associate professor at the University of Kentucky, also calls slip-on walking shoes a “huge step up” from flip-flops and slides.

Slip-on walking shoes aren’t for everyone. The fit can still throw some people off, and some simply prefer the tighter feel that laces deliver. But if you want travel-friendly shoes you can toss on in a second, these are a solid choice. As people who value quality, supportive footwear, Men’s Health editors have put in plenty of miles in slip-on walking shoes. The below check all the boxes.

The On Cloud 6 is an excellent example of how good a slip-on shoe can be. You can get in and out of this sneaker with no issue thanks to its wide opening, but the shoe’s elastic “speed” laces and sockliner create a snug fit once you’re in. (Those elastic laces can be adjusted to find your perfect fit.)

The sneaker uses Zero-Gravity CloudTec, which is On’s signature lightweight foam with hollow pods below for a cushioned, yet stable, feel underfoot. (Just be aware that those pods are prone to trapping small pebbles and debris.) A built-in flexible plate, called a Speedboard, helps push you forward with each step. This shoe also comes in a waterproof option, if you’re into rainy strolls. With a wide range of color options and an unobnoxious design, you can pair these with just about anything.

It’s tough to find a quality shoe under $100 right now, let alone one from a big brand. But the Adidas Cloudfoam Cuxxion Sock Shoes have some colorways under $50, making them an ideal choice for budget shoppers who don’t want to mess with laces.

This shoe uses Adidas’ signature Cloudfoam technology at the midsole for a plush, cushioned feel. Its Adiwear outsole is durable and grippy enough for most needs, too. But the real standout in this shoe is its elastic sock upper. It molds to your foot to create a surprisingly snug feel, even for narrow feet. The elastic sock collar supports that secure feel, although it may be too tight for people with wider ankles. The engineered knit upper is highly breathable, lowering the odds you’ll end your walk with sweaty feet. We appreciate the oversized pull tabs in front and back, making the process of getting these on and off seamless.

Feet come in all sizes, making it tough to find a slip-on shoe that works for everyone—and putting adjustable features at a premium. The Nike Pegasus 42 EasyOn has a specialized EasyOn lacing and bungee system up top to help you get the level of tightness you want, before locking it into place. (The lock and bungee combination takes some practice to get right at first.)

The shoe has a collapsible heel that springs back into place once you’re in, making the process of getting these on seamless. It’s also crafted with the same ReactX foam and Air Zoom unit as the standard—and popular—Nike Pegasus 42 running shoe, delivering an energetic feel under your feet. Convenient pull tabs at the heel sit flush against the shoe when they’re not in use, adding to the shoe’s overall sleekness.

Read More: Best Walking Shoes for Men Over 50

Stability shoes are designed to guide your foot with each step and prevent too much inward rolling as you go. But choosing a stability shoe usually means sacrificing a high level of cushioning, since a shoe that feels too plush may not be overly supportive. Hoka’s Skyward Laceless manages to create a stable, locked-in feel while still delivering plenty of the brand’s signature cushioning underfoot.

The Skyward Laceless has a stretchy upper that gently hugs your foot, creating a sock-like feel. The ankle and instep are equally snug, which can be a good or bad thing, depending on your foot size and width. This shoe has plenty of foam below for a slightly bouncy feel, but it still corrects your stride as you go. The integrated tongue pull tab is a nice touch, making for easier entry.

The Under Armour SlipSpeed Mega is packed with features you won’t find in most slip-on walking shoes, creating a versatile, unique sneaker. For starters, this shoe converts from a sneaker design to a recovery slipper with the help of a collapsible heel. (Under Armour refers to this as going from “speed mode” to “slip mode.”)

The shoe skips elastic laces or a sockliner upper in favor of Under Armour’s specialized BOA fit system, a 12-point dial that you can turn to adjust the width across the midfoot. The wide base creates a stable feel, while lots of foam cushioning underfoot delivers a plushness you’ll appreciate. A heads-up: This shoe is slightly heavier than others at 11.7 ounces. That’s a difference you may start to feel on long walks.

After a grueling workout, it feels borderline pampering to slide into the right recovery shoe. The Kane Footwear Active Recovery Shoe is armed with features that should make it a fixture in your gym bag.

This slip-on has strong arch support and a slight rocker shape to help ease pressure on the bottom of your feet as you walk. Internal nodes in the footbed help to promote blood flow and circulation down below, while the shoe’s surprisingly secure design helps prevent slipping. The Active Recovery Shoe is water-resistant with an airy design that allows you to take this in and out of the gym shower without ending up with sopping feet. Heel tabs in back make it simple to get in and out.

Merrell is known for its rugged, outdoor footwear and hiking shoes. While the Merrell Jungle Moc isn’t exactly a hiking shoe, it’s a solid option when you want good traction, whether you’re navigating rocky ground or a slippery surface. The Jungle Moc has been a bestseller for years, with its simple slip-on design and high level of cushioning.

Dual side stretch panels and an exaggerated heel tab make it simple to get in and out of these shoes. The suede upper is breathable, but water-resistant to keep you dry in nearly all conditions. The Jungle Moc has a cushioned EVA midsole for stability and comfort, too. While these shoes are easy to get on, the curved heel makes it harder to slide out—just something to be aware of.

Clogs admittedly aren’t the right style for everyone—some offer less support than sneakers and may slip around more than a standard shoe. But the sleek Crocs Dylan Clog is a solid option for people who want a clog style without some of the common issues that come with it.

The Dylan Clog has a deep heel cup to help lock your foot in, lowering the risk it’ll move around as you step. It’s also made from one piece of Croslite (Crocs’ signature material) to prevent wear and tear over time. This shoe looks like leather thanks to its subtle pebbled texture, but it’s water-resistant and dries quickly when wet. The only major downside is that it’s not very breathable in front. If you’re prone to sweaty toes, this may not be the shoe for you.

Not all shoes are created equal, but the best slip-on walking shoes have all of the supportive features you’ll find in standard lace-up walking shoes. “You mostly get what you pay for in these,” says Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California. He suggests taking a pass at dirt-cheap slip-on walking shoes. “The cheaper ones are not going to provide enough support in the long run, even if they might feel good at first,” Graves says. “There should be enough structure to support your arch and the midsole should be firm and not too flimsy.”

Many high-quality slip-on walking shoes provide similar comfort to regular sneakers. Look for elements like a breathable upper, pull tabs to make them easy to get on and off, and a roomy toe box. Structured heel panels and extra padding in this area help to keep your foot secure, even without standard laces.

Traction for slip-on walking shoes will vary depending on the type of shoe you choose. Most will offer decent traction—meaning, enough so you don’t feel like you’re slipping on wet or damp pavement. But a more rugged shoe like the Merrell Jungle Moc has a grippier sole to help provide extra traction over rockier ground.

Yes, slip-on walking shoes can provide arch support. If this is an important quality for you, look for features like contoured footbeds and a stable midsole. You’ll also want a shoe that fits well and stays put once it’s on to ensure your arch support is consistent. “Make sure that you're not getting them too loose just to make it easier to slide on and off—then you'll be sacrificing support,” Graves says.

To find the best men’s slip-on walking shoes, MH editors tested the most recent and popular pairs on the market, evaluating each for support, comfort, and traction. Because these shoes are designed for walking, not just comfort, durability was also a key factor. To round things out, we consulted three podiatrists for their input on how to evaluate a slip-on walking shoe, along with the value of this style. Based on their advice and our experience, we chose these slip-on walking shoes.

#4896. 12 Health Benefits of Pilates That Make It Worth the Hype, According to a Physical Therapist

Say hello to core strength, better endurance, and less back pain.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

There’s a reason Pilates has a reputation of being a leg-shaking, muscle-quaking workout. But it’s more than just a hard workout—it ended up being a total game changer for my health.

As an orthopedic physical therapist and conditioning coach, I’ve built my life around strength, health, and movement. Sports have always been central to who I am—running, weightlifting, and higher-intensity training used to be my norm—though my body hasn’t always kept up.

Then, last summer, I took my first reformer Pilates class at Bodyrok, a 45-minute full-body group fitness class. It was humbling—I engaged muscles I rarely worked in traditional strength training sessions (hello, core) and tackled moves I had never done before. But slowing down and focusing on controlled movements also felt surprisingly satisfying.

After eight months of consistent reformer Pilates classes (plus running and strength training sessions), I finally understood the hype. It has strengthened my core and pelvic muscles, improved circulation to alleviate pain, and eased inflammation. Plus, it complements my sport performance because it targets stabilizer muscles and mobility.

Here’s why both mat and reformer Pilates truly deliver, according to research.

Of all the benefits Pilates offers, it’s most famous for its focus on core strength—a key foundation for nearly everything we do, from lifting a baby and swinging a golf club to simply maintaining good posture at a desk. More specifically, Pilates targets the deep stabilizing muscles of the core, including the often overlooked transverse abdominis, as well as the rectus abdominis, or your six-pack muscles.

Want to pair Pilates and strength training in a streamlined way? Try the Women’s Health+ Pilates x Lift workout plan, a four-week program that gives you the best of both modalities to build muscle, improve mobility, and protect your joints.

Pilates combines controlled movements that lengthen and stretch your muscles, helping improve flexibility and range of motion within a joint. In fact, just six weeks of Pilates may improve functional mobility, according to research in the Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies. By working your muscles through their full range of motion, Pilates makes everyday activities like climbing stairs and bending down to tie your shoes feel easier and more fluid.

Most of us spend hours hunched over computers, then move straight to our phones or the TV, which can wreak total havoc on our posture. Fortunately, Pilates can undo those habits by strengthening the core and upper back, stabilizing the shoulders, and opening up the chest.

Research supports these benefits: A 2024 systematic review published in Archives of Rehabilitation Research and Clinical Translation found that after eight weeks of Pilates, sedentary women showed improvements in both posture and their ability to perform daily activities. Pilates also emphasizes proper form and alignment, so you’re constantly practicing better posture during your workouts—a habit that, with practice, can naturally carry over into everyday life.

Pilates isn’t just about your core—it’s a full-body workout that fires up multiple muscle groups at once, building strength from head to toe, especially when using a reformer for added resistance. In fact, a 2025 randomized trial published in Nature found that women who practiced reformer Pilates for 60 minutes three times per week for eight weeks saw measurable gains in muscle mass, grip strength, and body composition.

Research also shows that Pilates can boost muscular endurance, or the ability of your muscles to perform repeated contractions or maintain a position against resistance over time.

What truly sets Pilates apart, though, is its focus on the smaller stabilizing muscles most people ignore, which play a key role in controlled, efficient movement. Because of this, Pilates can enhance functional movement patterns, making it a secret weapon for better performance and fewer injuries.

The functional strength and stability aspects of Pilates make it an excellent complement to heavy lifting (which you should still do two to three times a week to develop bone density, improve metabolic health, and develop muscular power). That’s because a strong core protects against injury (like lower back pain) and helps you maintain good form even when handling a heavy barbell, per 2023 research in Healthcare.

Pilates is all about syncing breath, focus, and fluid movement, encouraging a deep connection between the mind and body. Each exercise requires careful attention to form, encouraging intentional, controlled movement that can feel almost meditative. This mindfulness, combined with the focus on strengthening the mind-body connection (the two-way link between your mental state and physical health), naturally supports mental well-being.

Because breathing is central to Pilates, it can also reduce stress and promote a sense of calm. As a matter of fact, doing Pilates just once a week for an hour over the span of three months can improve anxiety, depression, and stress, according to 2025 research in Healthcare.

About 80 percent of adults in the U.S. will experience lower back pain at some point in their lives, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH). But Pilates can help relieve that pain, as it stabilizes the core and improves posture, according to a 2025 study in the Irish Journal of Medical Science. The study had 66 participants ages 18 to 65 with lower back pain either do Pilates three times a week or a home exercise program (involving stretching, strengthening, and mobility exercises) for eight weeks. The group that did Pilates experienced improvements in pain relief, functional disability, and quality of life, compared to those who did the home exercise program.

Additionally, a 2022 review in the Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy looked at 118 trials to find out the best exercise options for reducing pain and disability in adults with chronic lower back pain. It looked at aerobic, strength, combined aerobic and strength, core-based, McKenzie (movements designed to relieve musculoskeletal pain), Pilates, stretching, and mind-body exercise. It found that Pilates, core-based, and mind-body exercise were the best for reducing pain—but Pilates had the highest likelihood for lowering pain and disability.

Your balance decreases as you age, according to the NIH, but not if you do something about it. A 2021 study in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health observed the effects of Pilates training on balance and fall risk in older women. It had 50 women over 60 years old either do two Pilates sessions for three months, or no exercise outside of everyday activities. Before and after training, the women did exercises like the single-leg stance and Timed Up and Go (where you stand from a sitting position, walk, and then do it in reverse), and other tests. The group that did Pilates improved their balance and lowered their fall risk more than the group that didn’t exercise.

One 2021 review of literature on exercise and longevity in Aging shows how regular exercise can slow down cellular aging—and Pilates is a great fitness modality to support strength, mobility, and confidence as we age. Since it’s low-impact and lower intensity, it can help build strength without overstressing your joints, making it a sustainable workout for now and the future.

In fact, in a 2025 study in the Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies, 24 adults age 76, on average, either did 20 weeks of an online Pilates program or no exercise. Their balance, core stability, and functional fitness were tested with exercises like the single-leg stance, 6-minute walk test, and core muscle strength and stability tests. The study found that the Pilates program improved balance, cardiorespiratory endurance, and core strength in older adults, especially compared to the group that didn’t exercise.

Both mat and reformer Pilates can provide all of the benefits above, but they also have some of their own distinct draws. Reformer Pilates, specifically, can be really useful for training muscle patterns in a gentle way—by using springs for resistance rather than gravity, WH previously reported. (Think: footwork while lying down on a reformer rather than a standing squat with a barbell.) As a result, you’re able to relax more into each move, making it a lower-impact workout.

And with its moving carriage, the Pilates reformer can be a valuable tool for building greater balance and stability, as it creates a greater challenge than you’d get on solid ground with a mat workout.

What’s more, a reformer can help support someone rehabbing from an injury—particularly because it can help correct misaligned movement patterns more effectively than simply completing a bodyweight move.

Perhaps the best part of any Pilates modality? It’s for anyone and everyone, no matter your age or fitness level. While some Pilates classes (i.e., those using reformers) can be intimidating and costly, you actually don’t need any equipment to get started. Pilates can be done with just your body and a workout mat, and you can even replicate reformer-style moves using sliders, foam rollers, and towels.

No matter how you practice, the focus on controlled movement and mindful breathing makes Pilates a real game changer for athletic performance and holistic wellness. Trust me, I speak from experience.

#4893. What You Should Know About Exercising When Bone Density Is a Concern

Osteopenia or osteoporosis doesn’t have to sideline your workouts. Here’s what to do, how to modify, and when to back off.

You might have heard that being active is a good idea when you have osteopenia or osteoporosis, conditions marked by lower-than-normal bone density. But when you’re exercising specifically to improve bone health, some types of exercise may be more helpful than others. Before lacing up your sneakers, there are a few things to know.

“When patients ask me what they can do to preserve and protect their bone health, consistent weight bearing and resistance exercises are the first things I recommend,” says Nicole Leung, MD, director of the Osteoporosis and Bone Health Program at NYU Langone Health in New York City. “Bone is a living tissue, so it adapts to mechanical load through remodeling.”

When bone tissue is stressed via physical activity, your body responds by making more bone, helping strengthen the tissue. Exercise also lowers the activity of cells that dissolve and break down old bone. That combo helps preserve or even improve your bone mineral density, regardless of your health status. Exercise may slow or even prevent the progression of osteoporosis; if you have osteoporosis already, it can help you maintain the bone you have and reduce your risk for falls and fractures.

A bone-density diagnosis doesn’t mean you have to give up exercise—but your routine should reflect your fracture risk and health history. Here’s what Dr. Leung recommends for choosing activities, adapting your routine, and knowing when to check with your doctor before making major changes.

There are a few types of activities that make up a bone-friendly exercise plan, and it’s important to get the right amount of each. Here are the types of exercise to do regularly.

These are exercises where you’re on your feet and putting force on your muscles and bones as they work against gravity. Depending on factors like your age, fitness level, and bone mineral density, these activities can include:

People working to maintain their bone health should do these sorts of activities for 30 to 60 minutes, three to five days per week, according to the American College of Sports Medicine.

As for activities like swimming and cycling, they’re great for getting your heart pumping—but because they’re low-impact, they won’t do much for your bones. That said, feel free to do them in addition to your weight-bearing exercises if you enjoy them.

Lifting (relatively) heavy things works your muscles and helps build bone density. This includes free weights, machines, resistance bands, or body weight exercises like squats or push-ups. Aim for two to three strength sessions per week, and don’t be afraid to gradually go heavier (with your doctor’s okay). Pushing yourself to 70 to 90 percent of your max effort may deliver a bigger bone boost than lifting lighter weights, research suggests.

Having osteoporosis makes you more prone to fractures after falls, but you can strengthen your balance—and reduce your chances for a broken bone—with exercises like yoga, tai chi, or Pilates. “Any exercise where you have to shift your body weight side to side and forward and back can be very helpful for your stabilizing muscles,” Dr. Leung says. She recommends working balance exercises into your schedule a few times per week. Find safe modifications if you’re worried about falling, like holding onto a sturdy chair or touching a wall.

Whether you’ve been exercising for years, are just starting out, or are returning to a routine after a long hiatus, Dr. Leung advises paying attention to your posture, avoiding exercise when you’re overly exhausted, and increasing intensity gradually. Older women who are new to exercise can still do resistance training, she says, but may need to start at a slower pace and under supervision.

Despite the overall benefits of exercise, you still need to be careful, particularly when you have osteoporosis. Certain activities can set the stage for potential spine fractures, so before starting an exercise program, decide with your doctor or other qualified professional what is and isn’t safe for you.

According to the International Osteoporosis Foundation, you may need to limit or avoid moves that involve:

Yoga, while helpful for balance, can involve poses that put your spine at risk (like forward bends, deep twists, plow pose, shoulder stand, and pigeon pose). If you decide to give it a try, choose a class where the teacher can offer safe modifications, Dr. Leung says. It’s also best to steer clear of activities that come with a high risk of falling from above standing height, like skiing or horseback riding, she adds.

When it comes to stressing your bones, it’s possible to get too much of a good thing. “Overburdening your bone can actually lead to stress fractures,” Dr. Leung says. If you do prolonged intense weight-bearing and high-impact exercises like jogging or jumping rope, avoid scheduling them on back-to-back days. Alternate those workouts with activities like strength training, or have an active recovery day where you walk or do yoga or tai chi, she recommends.

Make it a point to stay active even after you’ve completed the day’s workout. According to Dr. Leung, non-exercise activities like casual walking or doing chores may help to maintain bone density when compared to sedentary behavior. Stroll over to chat with a coworker at their desk during a break, take the stairs when you can, or walk while you call a friend instead of sitting. A few minutes here and there can really add up.

Any new or worsening bone or spine pain is a warning sign to stop exercising and contact your doctor. You should also call your doctor if you fall while exercising, notice that you’ve had height loss, or if your spine appears curved, which could be signs of a spinal fracture. And always stop exercising and seek medical attention if you experience other severe symptoms like dizziness, faintness, or chest pain.

Consistency counts. People with low bone density who stay active over several months tend to see the greatest bone-health benefits, studies show. Choose activities you enjoy, build up gradually, and find a rhythm you can sustain. The goal isn’t to nail every workout—it’s to keep movement in your life.

#4892. On Wants You to Feel Your Softest Ride Yet

The Cloudsurfer 3 is built to make everyday runs feel smooth and effortless, even as the miles add up.

Just because you run doesn’t necessarily mean that you’re up on running shoe innovation. In recent years, there have been notable improvements in propulsion and efficiency, thanks to additions like carbon-fiber plates, smart sensors, and midsoles that promise high energy return. What’s more important than these buzzy words is: How do the shoes feel?

After all, you can have footwear designed by rocket scientists, but if you’re uncomfortable with every step, your run will be a slog, no matter the distance. You want your shoe to make the ride feel soft, which is why the On Cloudsurfer 3 stands out over so many others.

On running shoes have always been distinguished by their trademark hollow pods— the “clouds” that are specifically engineered to help create a softer underfoot experience and give the brand its unmistakable look. In the Cloudsurfer 3, On’s CloudTec Phase™ allows those pods to compress in sequence, helping absorb impact and create a smoother transition from heel to toe. This isn’t just another update to On’s running shoe line. With breakthrough Swiss engineering working beneath every step, the Cloudsurfer 3 delivers the brand’s softest ride yet.

An option for everyday and recovery runs as well as longer training sessions, the Cloudsurfer 3 combines CloudTec® Phase with On’s brand-new SurrealTM Superfoam. According to the brand’s internal testing, the pairing provides 15.5 percent deeper compression—and therefore more impact absorption—than the superfoam alone. The result is a softer landing that can help daily miles feel easier on the legs, particularly over long distances.

According to the same internal testing, the Cloudsurfer 3 is also predicted to deliver a 9.9 percent improvement in smooth-ride sensation. That figure reflects the way the reimagined CloudTec® Phase orientation enhances the rolling motion of the foot, helping each step flow more naturally into the next from landing to toe-off.

You’re also getting a newly engineered mesh upper in the Cloudsurfer 3, which provides a secure fit that adapts to your foot while still offering breathability and support. That breathability helps keep heat and moisture from building up, reducing the conditions that can lead to chafing, blisters, and hot spots.

Even the cushioning around the collar and tongue has been updated, so you get a cloud-like feel as soon as you slip them on. It doesn’t hurt that the Cloudsurfer 3 looks cool, too.

Together, these innovations give runners what they want from an everyday shoe: a natural feel, reliable performance, and lasting comfort. The result is a smoother ride, whether you’re going long or heading out for a quick training run.

That softer feel is a big deal, considering a 2025 study found that runners who perceived their shoes as more cushioned had a lower risk of running-related injury. When a shoe feels right, you’re less likely to think about every step—or adjust the way you’re moving to compensate for discomfort. That allows you to settle into your natural stride and focus on the run itself.

Enjoyment is a major factor, too. Wearing a shoe like the Cloudsurfer 3, with its focus on cushioning, responsiveness, and comfort, can be key to unlocking your best run yet—and enjoying yourself along the way. When that happens, even a hard run can feel softer, mile after mile.

Elizabeth Millard is a freelance writer focusing on health, wellness, fitness, and food.
